# # Refactor Orchestration: Spring Kafka Listener Container Threading Model

## Context

Spring Kafka's listener container threading model needs refactoring from
single-threaded KafkaMessageListenerContainer to ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer
with configurable concurrency. This change touches three repositories:

- spring-framework provides core messaging abstractions
- spring-kafka implements Kafka-specific listener containers
- spring-boot autoconfigures and exposes properties for listener containers

The dependency chain: spring-framework -> spring-kafka -> spring-boot

## Task

Produce a topologically sorted execution plan for this refactoring across all
three repos, identifying ordering constraints, parallelization opportunities,
and breaking changes.

## Repos in Workspace

- `/workspace/spring-framework/` -- Spring Framework 6.0.11 (upstream abstractions)
- `/workspace/spring-kafka/` -- Spring Kafka 3.0.9 (primary implementation)
- `/workspace/spring-boot/` -- Spring Boot 3.1.2 (autoconfiguration consumer)

## Expected Output

Write `/workspace/REFACTOR_PLAN.md` containing:

1. A numbered list of repos in the order they should be updated
2. Dependency graph (who depends on whom)
3. Parallelization annotations (which steps can run concurrently)
4. Breaking vs. compatible change annotations per step
5. Risk assessment for each repo change

# Refactor Orchestration Plan: Spring Kafka Listener Container Threading Model

## Overview

Migrating from single-threaded `KafkaMessageListenerContainer` to `ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer` with configurable concurrency across three repositories in dependency order.

**Dependency chain (upstream → downstream):**

```
spring-framework  →  spring-kafka  →  spring-boot
```

- `spring-framework` (v6.0.11) provides `AsyncTaskExecutor`, `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor`, `TaskDecorator`, and related threading abstractions consumed by spring-kafka.
- `spring-kafka` (v3.0.9) owns the listener-container hierarchy: [`AbstractMessageListenerContainer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/AbstractMessageListenerContainer.java?L69-L71) → [`KafkaMessageListenerContainer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/KafkaMessageListenerContainer.java?L165-L166) / [`ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer.java?L62), plus [`ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/config/ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory.java?L46-L47).
- `spring-boot` (v3.1.2) autoconfigures the container via [`KafkaAnnotationDrivenConfiguration`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-boot--v3.1.2/-/blob/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/kafka/KafkaAnnotationDrivenConfiguration.java?L50-L130), [`ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactoryConfigurer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-boot--v3.1.2/-/blob/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/kafka/ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactoryConfigurer.java?L159-L189), and [`KafkaProperties`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-boot--v3.1.2/-/blob/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/kafka/KafkaProperties.java?L977) (which already exposes `spring.kafka.listener.concurrency`).

---

## 1. Execution Order (Topologically Sorted)

| Step | Repo | Deliverable |
|------|------|-------------|
| 1 | `spring-framework` | Executor API enhancements (optional; only if new threading primitives are needed) |
| 2 | `spring-kafka` | Core container refactoring — promote `ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer` as default |
| 3 | `spring-boot` | Autoconfiguration update — expose and wire any new concurrency properties |

---

## 2. Dependency Graph

```
spring-framework (v6.0.11)
  │
  │  provides: AsyncTaskExecutor, SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor, TaskDecorator,
  │             SmartLifecycle, ApplicationContext integration
  ▼
spring-kafka (v3.0.9)
  │
  │  provides: ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer, KafkaMessageListenerContainer,
  │             AbstractMessageListenerContainer, ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory,
  │             AbstractKafkaListenerContainerFactory, ContainerProperties
  ▼
spring-boot (v3.1.2)
       provides: KafkaAutoConfiguration, KafkaAnnotationDrivenConfiguration,
                 ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactoryConfigurer,
                 KafkaProperties.Listener (spring.kafka.listener.*)
```

Key coupling points:
- [`ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer.doStart()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer.java?L210-L235) creates one child `KafkaMessageListenerContainer` per concurrency slot, assigning a `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor` per child (with prefix `beanName + "-C-"`) unless a custom executor is injected via `ContainerProperties.setListenerTaskExecutor`.
- [`ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory.initializeContainer()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/config/ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory.java?L80-L92) applies endpoint-level concurrency (from `@KafkaListener(concurrency=...)`) with fallback to factory-level concurrency.
- [`ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactoryConfigurer.configureListenerFactory()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-boot--v3.1.2/-/blob/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/kafka/ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactoryConfigurer.java?L173-L189) maps `KafkaProperties.Listener.getConcurrency()` → `factory.setConcurrency(...)` at line 176.

---

## 3. Per-Step Work, Parallelization, and Change Annotations

### Step 1 — `spring-framework` | **PARALLEL-SAFE** | **COMPATIBLE** | Risk: LOW

No upstream dependency; can proceed immediately and independently. spring-kafka and spring-boot are blocked only if new framework API is actually introduced.

**Scope:** Additive changes to the `spring-core` task package ([`AsyncTaskExecutor`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-core/src/main/java/org/springframework/core/task/AsyncTaskExecutor.java), [`SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-core/src/main/java/org/springframework/core/task/SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor.java)). If no new executor API is required, this step is skipped entirely.

**Risk rationale:** `AsyncTaskExecutor` has been stable since Spring 2.0. No listener-container classes live here; `GenericMessageListenerContainer` and the full Kafka hierarchy are in spring-kafka.

---

### Step 2 — `spring-kafka` | **SEQUENTIAL after Step 1 (if needed), else PARALLEL** | **PARTIALLY BREAKING** | Risk: MEDIUM-HIGH

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [`listener/KafkaMessageListenerContainer.java`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/KafkaMessageListenerContainer.java) | No public-API change; remains child-container implementation |
| [`listener/ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer.java`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer.java) | Promote as default container. Optionally add `ThreadPoolTaskExecutor` support via `ContainerProperties` |
| [`listener/AbstractMessageListenerContainer.java`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/AbstractMessageListenerContainer.java) | Add `getMaxConcurrency()`/`setMaxConcurrency()` if dynamic scaling is in scope |
| [`config/ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory.java`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/config/ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory.java) | Already correct; validate endpoint vs. factory concurrency precedence |
| [`config/AbstractKafkaListenerContainerFactory.java`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/config/AbstractKafkaListenerContainerFactory.java) | Wire new executor-pool options if added |

**Breaking changes:**
- **BREAKING** — Thread name change: replacing direct `KafkaMessageListenerContainer` use with `ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer(concurrency=1)` changes thread naming from `consumer-0` to `consumer-0-C-0`. Tests asserting exact thread names will fail.
- **COMPATIBLE** — `clientIdSuffix`: `alwaysClientIdSuffix=true` (default) already appends `-0` even at `concurrency=1`; existing `false` users are unaffected.
- **COMPATIBLE** — Partition capping: [`doStart()` already warns and caps `concurrency` to `topicPartitions.length`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer.java?L216-L221) when explicit partitions are assigned.
- **COMPATIBLE** — Auth-exception restart: [`childStopped()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-kafka--v3.0.9/-/blob/spring-kafka/src/main/java/org/springframework/kafka/listener/ConcurrentMessageListenerContainer.java?L352-L370) already uses `this.concurrency == this.stoppedContainers`; no change required.

**Risk rationale:** `KafkaMessageListenerContainer` is a 2,000+ line class with a complex `ListenerConsumer` inner class; offset-commit and thread-pinning semantics must not regress. `doStart()` and `doStop()` both run under `lifecycleMonitor`; executor pool management must not introduce lock contention. Integration tests against a real broker at `concurrency=1`, `2`, and `N > partitions` are mandatory.

**Internal parallelization opportunities within Step 2:**
- Executor-pool integration (new `ContainerProperties` API) is independent of partition-distribution and client-id-suffix changes.
- Test updates for thread-naming are independent of functional changes.

---

### Step 3 — `spring-boot` | **SEQUENTIAL after Step 2 release; dev work PARALLEL** | **COMPATIBLE** | Risk: LOW

Developer work can begin immediately using a spring-kafka SNAPSHOT; the artifact must not be released before spring-kafka GA ships.

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [`KafkaProperties.java` (`Listener` inner class, line 977)](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-boot--v3.1.2/-/blob/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/kafka/KafkaProperties.java?L974-L984) | `spring.kafka.listener.concurrency` already present. Add `executor-type` (SIMPLE/THREAD_POOL) and `thread-name-prefix` only if new spring-kafka API exposes them |
| [`ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactoryConfigurer.java` (line 176)](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-boot--v3.1.2/-/blob/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/kafka/ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactoryConfigurer.java?L173-L189) | Already maps `concurrency`; add mappings for any new properties |
| [`KafkaAnnotationDrivenConfiguration.java`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-boot--v3.1.2/-/blob/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/kafka/KafkaAnnotationDrivenConfiguration.java) | No structural changes expected |
| `additional-spring-configuration-metadata.json` | Add descriptions for any new properties |

**Breaking changes:** None. `spring.kafka.listener.concurrency` already exists and already supports `> 1`. Any new properties are additive with safe defaults. The autoconfigured `kafkaListenerContainerFactory` bean type remains `ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory`.

**Risk rationale:** spring-boot's Kafka autoconfiguration is a thin property-mapping layer. The existing `configurer` wiring already calls `factory.setConcurrency(...)` unconditionally when the property is set. Main risk is integration tests that assume `concurrency=1` default behavior if that default changes in spring-kafka.

---

## 4. Parallelization Summary

```
t=0 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►
     Step 1: spring-framework  ─────────────────────────────────────────────
     Step 2: spring-kafka       (starts at t=0 if Step 1 adds no new API) ──
                                    │
                                    └─ Step 3 dev work: starts at t=0       
                                       (SNAPSHOT dep on spring-kafka)        
                                       release gates on spring-kafka GA ─────

Minimum critical path (no framework changes):
  [spring-kafka refactor] → [spring-boot release update]

With framework changes:
  [spring-framework] → [spring-kafka] → [spring-boot]
```

---

## 5. Risk Assessment Summary

| Repo | Risk | Primary Concerns |
|------|------|-----------------|
| `spring-framework` | **LOW** | Additive-only; `AsyncTaskExecutor` interface stable since 2.0. Skip if no new API needed. |
| `spring-kafka` | **MEDIUM-HIGH** | Thread-safety under `lifecycleMonitor`; `ListenerConsumer` inner-class complexity; rebalance side-effects at higher concurrency; thread-name contract change breaks tests. |
| `spring-boot` | **LOW** | Thin mapping layer; `concurrency` property already present and wired; all changes additive. |

---

## 6. Recommended Release Sequence

1. Cut a spring-framework SNAPSHOT (or skip if no new executor API is needed).
2. Develop spring-kafka changes against the SNAPSHOT; run integration tests at `concurrency=1`, `2`, and `N > partitions`.
3. Publish spring-kafka RC; update spring-boot to depend on the RC.
4. Validate spring-boot autoconfiguration integration tests.
5. Ship: **spring-framework GA → spring-kafka GA → spring-boot GA**.

---
